Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third session! The players are already out in the middle now. Usman Khawaja and David Warner are the two openers for Australia. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Here we go...
.. THIRD INNINGS ...

Pakistan, on the other hand, showed great resilience especially their openers who looked solid and were able to tire the Aussie bowlers. Abdullah Shafique lost his patience and lost his wicket while skipper Shan Masood played a quick-fire knock but he too went back to the hut before Stumps on Day 2. However, Imam-ul-Haq continued to bat in his own way and built up a good partnership with Babar Azam and also registered a gritty half-century, but towards the end of the first session, they lost their way and three wickets fell in quick succession putting them on the back foot. After that, there were a couple of good contributions from Saud Shakeel and Agha Salman, but that too failed to get them past the follow-on score. However, the Aussies decided not to enforce it. Join us at 12.50 pm IST (7.20 am GMT) for the final session.

Pat Cummins, the skipper of Australia is up for a chat. He says that Pakistan made them work hard and his side bowled pretty well but without much luck. Mentions that they are happy where they are at right now. Shares that it is a good wicket but there is enough when bowled in the right areas. Adds that there have been plenty of plays and misses so far in the game. Credits Pakistan for the way they batted and says that they left well. Ends by informing that Australia will not be enforcing the follow-on.

Australia have bowled out Pakistan and still leads by a huge margin of 216 runs. With that, Tea has been taken. Session Summary - 63 runs and 4 wickets in 23.5 overs. It was not easy but hard work finally paid off for the Aussies as they were excellent right from the start of Day 3. Initially, they struggled to get the first breakthrough, but Nathan Lyon provided it while Mitchell Starc ensured they had two wickets at Stumps on Day 2. Pat Cummins and Josh Hazlewood were brilliant while Starc was a bit wayward at times but produced a couple of magical deliveries, and they shared five wickets among themselves. Lyon also picked his 498th and 499th Test wickets while the big moment was when local boy, Mitchell Marsh got rid of the big fish, Babar Azam. Everyone was expecting Lyon to get his 500th scalp, but Travis Head wrapped things up for them.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Travis Head gets the last wicket and Nathan Lyon will have to wait until the second innings for his 500th Test wicket! Travis Head gives the ball air, on middle, and entices the batter to go for the big heave across the line. Shaheen Afridi accepts the invitation as he swings hard but the ball spins away a touch and he gets a top edge. The ball skies high in the air but only as far as mid on where Usman Khawaja settles under it and completes the catch with his fingers pointing downwards. Pakistan have been bowled out for 271 and Australia take the first-innings lead of 216 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session on Day 3! The two umpires make their way out to the middle as do the Aussies. Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel are all set to resume their innings for Pakistan. It will be Nathan Lyon to start the proceedings with the ball for Australia. All eyes will be on him as he is a couple of wickets away from 500 Test wickets. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

On the other hand, Pakistan will be pretty disappointed with how it all panned out in the second hour of play as they lost their last 3 wickets for just 15 runs. The visitors lost Khurram Shahzad early on Day 3 but the nightwatchman did what was asked of him to see off the tricky phase late on Day 2. Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam then got together to see off the early movement on offer and put on a decent stand to take the innings forward. Imam notched up his fifty and Babar was looking solid as well until a tentative prod led to his downfall. Imam followed suit as he ran out of patience before Sarfaraz Ahmed was undone by a searing delivery from Mitchell Starc. Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel did well to ensure that there were no more hiccups before the Lunch break. With the tail to follow and Pakistan currently trailing by 284 runs, a lot will rest on the shoulders of these two batters if they are to avoid the follow-on. Join us back at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session on Day 3.

After Pakistan took the honours in the first hour, Australia came roaring back and they will be the happier side at the Lunch interval! Australia were patient throughout the first session and have 4 wickets to show for their efforts. The hosts were disciplined with their lines and lengths right from the start and bowled fuller than they did on Day 2. Pat Cummins struck in the first over on Day 3 but then they were stalled by a gritty stand between Imam and Babar. The move to bring local boy Mitchell Marsh into the attack worked wonders for them as he got rid of Babar before Nathan Lyon foxed Imam to make him his 498th Test victim. Mitchell Starc joined in on the fun as well to put Pakistan in more trouble. With not much batting left to come and the second new ball only 2 overs away, Australia would want to wrap up the innings as quickly as possible in the second session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 3! The Australian players are making their way out in the middle and spread out to take their respective field positions. Imam-ul-Haq walks out along with 'nightwatchman', Khurram Shahzad to continue the batting for Pakistan. Pat Cummins to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

On the other hand, it was a much-improved performance from Pakistan on Day 2. Although, the pacers had some difficulties in the first session, they came back strong after Lunch as the debutant, Aamer Jamal took four wickets and completed his six-wicket haul which helped his team to seize the Aussies under 500. After coming on to bat, the Pakistani openers batted brilliantly, resisting the swing of the new ball, but Abdullah Shafique was dismissed as he lost his patience. The skipper, Shan Masood helped his team to score some quick runs but could not stick around till Stumps.  The onus will be on Imam-ul-Haq to anchor as he has faced a lot of deliveries to judge the pitch. They still have a couple of experienced batters like Babar Azam and Sarfaraz Ahmed to light up some hopes for their fans. They will try to sustain the Day 3 sessions without losing many wickets, because that is the only way they can steal the match from Aussie's pocket. Will Pakistan be able to take the match under their control? We shall find out soon, as the first ball is not far away.

Australia are still ahead in the race against the Shaheens, as Day 2 was a good day for the Aussies. On Day 2, they managed to score more than they expected, all thanks to the local boy Mitchell Marsh who scored 90 runs off 107 deliveries. They also got 2 wickets in the second inning which will give them an extra boost for the Day 3 sessions. Their bowling unit was phenomenal, especially Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, as both opened their account for getting wickets. The skipper, Pat Cummins, was also very economical and was able to put pressure on the opposing batters. On Day 3, Aussie's bowling unit will try their best to dismiss the top and middle order, to make sure they don't lose their grip from the match.

Right then, that is it from a competitive Day 2 of this 'West Test' where Australia are still ahead in the game but Pakistan showed good fight to stay in it. Now, the focus shifts onto the 'Moving Day' where we might see this game pick up pace and move towards a result. Day 3 will begin on 16th December, Saturday at 7.50 am IST (2.20 am GMT), but as you know, you can always join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Alex Carey is in for a flash interview. He says that he would have liked a couple of wickets more. Mentions that this is a total they would have been happy to take before the start of play on Day 1. Reckons that it is a big morning on Day 3 and hopes that they can get the ball in the right areas. States that they will have a look tonight at what their lengths were. Feels that both teams could have bowled fuller. Credits the Pakistan bowlers for the way they bowled this morning and their openers for absorbing the pressure. On the effectiveness of Mitchell Marsh on this surface, he replies that Marsh pitches the ball up and has a good skill-set to get the ball wobbling.

Australia, on the other had, would have been happy with their total considering the conditions, but the only unfortunate thing for them was that Mitchell Marsh missed out on his well-deserved hundred. They dominated the first session again as they added 130 runs to their overnight total but just lost their way a bit after Lunch. The hosts would have expected to make early inroads but even though their pacers were right on the money, they couldn't get any rewards as luck favoured the batters. However, they kept going at the batters and finally Nathan Lyon provided them the crucial breakthrough in the last session. They allowed another partnership to grow, but Mitchell Starc got his first wicket of the summer by getting rid of the opposition skipper and will be looking to add to his tally on Day 3.

Pakistan started Day 2 just like they started the Test with their pacers being a bit wayward and allowing the batters to score easy runs. However, gradually they came back into the game and the two debutants shone with the ball. Aamer Jamal was the pick of the bowlers as he picked up wickets on both sides of Lunch and ended with an exceptional six-wicket haul on debut which helped them bowl the Aussies out under 500. After coming on to bat, both the openers, Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique showed great resistance and technique to keep the Aussies out and saw out till Tea with some luck as well as they got beaten on a number of occasions. They added over 50 runs but right at the hour-mark in the third session, Shafique lost his patience which cost him his wicket but then skipper Shan Masood came in and played aggressively along with Imam. Masood lost his wicket right before stumps, but Imam remained unbeaten on 38 off 136 balls while; 'nightwatchman', Khurram Shahzad did his job to survive till the end.

A solid overall performance from Pakistan on Day 2, but they know that there is still a lot to do to challenge the hosts. It all started with the fantastic six-wicket haul from Aamer Jamal while their batters also have been pretty solid. Australia would have liked a few more wickets but they are still leading by 355 runs and will look to dominate proceedings on Day 3.

SESSION SUMMARY - 54 runs, 23.2 overs and 3 wickets. An absorbing session of red-ball cricket comes to an end and it was a session where Pakistan showed robust riposte. The visitors started well in the second session as Khurram Shahzad struck with the first delivery to remove Mitchell Marsh, who was closing in on a hundred. The other debutant, Aamer Jamal, then cleaned up the Aussie tail to finish with six wickets in his debut inning. In reply, it was a sedate start from the two Pakistani openers. Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq looked assured right from the start, showing good application. The Aussie pace attack did manage to beat the bat on several occasions, but Shafique and Imam did well to hang in there. The duo also managed to negate the threat during 3 overs from Nathan Lyon and ensured that Pakistan went to Tea with all ten wickets intact. That said, Pakistan cannot afford to let their guard down in the third session and must look to build on this start. Join us back at 12.50 pm IST (7.20 am GMT) for the proceedings of the final session.
